races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden
O'Driscolls Irish Whiskey Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a fade flag in recent runs; Denis Hogan's 7-pound claimer Mel Sheridan provides a small weight pull, but six runs without a win or place on good ground at this trip is a significant negative, and the horse's record suggests she finds little under pressure.|

runners_data.name: Variance
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up mare who has been consistently beaten in mid-to-rear-division finishes, with zero wins or places from five runs on similar going; Rory Cleary takes over but the form string of 7060-0 offers little encouragement at 7f on good.|

runners_data.name: Princess Chloe
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly whose most recent run produced a placed effort (2nd at 6f on good), giving her the most meaningful piece of recent form among the closers; Terry Casey's 7-pound claim is useful in a moderate handicap and she steps up to 7f for the first time since a solid fourth.|

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear, pushed into a midfield slot on the map simply because the field has too many closers for the pace map to accommodate; form includes a solid third from five runs on similar going and he handles Gowran (5 similar-going runs), but his style fit is compromised in this configuration.|

runners_data.name: Baby Basma
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, Ronan Whelan takes over and she will enjoy a totally uncontested lead; her win came over 5f on good at Gowran itself, so the step up to 7f on identical ground is the key question — if she stays, she is extremely well placed tactically.|

runners_data.name: Will Be King
runners_data.note: A veteran hold-up type whose true style is at the rear of the field; the aged 10-year-old has tongue tie and a pull as part of his routine, but Siobhan Rutledge rides, his going form is thin, and his fade flag alongside the positional compromise makes him very hard to recommend.|

runners_data.name: Liamo
runners_data.note: Prominent-tracking type with a genuine pace profile that suits tracking Baby Basma; Jimmy Dalton's 7-pound claim helps, he ran just 10 days ago and has shown consistency over 7-8f on good ground, making him one of the more logical pace beneficiaries.|

runners_data.name: Maker's Mark
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by inclination, placed into midfield on the map because of overcrowding at the rear; James Ryan rides, but form reads 90-050 with zero wins or places from nine runs on similar ground and the trip and conditions have not suited previously.|

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: Hold-up type by nature, placed further forward than ideal on the map; Michael Mulvany's stable has fired in three winners from 12 in the last 14 days which is the most compelling angle here, Wesley Joyce claims 3lb, and she has decent course form over sprint trips on good ground.|

runners_data.name: Romantic War
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer who has been running in much longer races (8-10f) and drops back to 7f having run just five days ago; Robyn Donaghue-Leahy's 7-pound claim is helpful but the fade flag, positional compromise, and very short turnaround make this a very speculative contender.|

runners_data.name: Garryowen Green
runners_data.note: A hold-up juvenile who has failed to place in five career runs, all in the 7-10f range on good-to-yielding; Nathan Crosse rides but the form string of 0-9900 with a consistent fade flag leaves little to work with, and the positional compromise further reduces the ceiling.|

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle — a booking that always commands attention — and she finished fifth most recently over 7f on good, with a third at 6f on good in her recent run string; Paul Flynn's yard is represented well and she is one of the more interesting closers if a run materialises.|

runners_data.name: Pocket Jacks
runners_data.note: Prominent type reunited with Ben Coen after a 43-day break; his last three runs show two placed efforts over 6-7f on good ground at competitive level, and his handy style makes him the most naturally suited prominent tracker to capitalise if Baby Basma is caught in the final furlong.|

runners_data.name: Stiorra
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning from a 296-day absence — a significant fitness concern — and though she has Jack Cleary's 5-pound claim and handled good ground when last seen, the long layoff combined with positional compromise and hold-up style moved to midfield makes her very hard to trust.|

runners_data.name: Hero Of The Hour
runners_data.note: Prominent-tracking type who has been consistently placed over sprint trips on good ground, and the veteran's profile of 635400 shows a recent fourth and placed effort; J M Sheridan rides and at 9 years old he knows his job, sitting close to Baby Basma to challenge in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Thumama Sands
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old with just three career runs, all on good or good-to-soft at 7f on this track and similar venues, finishing 12th, 11th, and 14th — a form string with no encouragement whatsoever; Adam Caffrey rides for Adrian McGuinness whose strike rate is decent but this horse offers nothing from the data.|

races.paceDynamic: Baby Basma is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 16-runner 7f handicap and, with no genuine rival likely to dispute the lead, she should be allowed to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop on good ground at Gowran. Pocket Jacks, Liamo, and Hero Of The Hour are the prominent types capable of tracking her through the first half of the race, giving the leader a small group to work with without a pace war breaking out. The field is loaded with hold-up horses — Roman Harry, Maker's Mark, Stiorra, Romantic War, Garryowen Green, Mini Cotai, and Will Be King are all natural hold-up types who cannot all operate from their preferred position and have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the closing kick from deep may be diluted by traffic and positional compromise. This shape — a controlled, uncontested pace set by Baby Basma — most favours prominent-to-handy trackers who can sit just off the leader and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out, rather than genuine hold-up closers who need a strong pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Baby Basma Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Baby Basma bowls along comfortably in front and Ronan Whelan sets a fair but measured tempo that drains hold-up horses without burning herself.
scenarios.body: Baby Basma dictates terms throughout, and the prominent trackers Pocket Jacks and Liamo sit close enough to challenge in the straight, with the closers arriving too late after covering extra ground through traffic. Prominent-to-handy profiles who can travel smoothly into the race and accelerate from two furlongs out are the clear beneficiaries of this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Baby Basma's pace is just honest enough to string the field out and the prominent horses tracking her can overhaul her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Pocket Jacks or Hero Of The Hour sit a length or two off the leader throughout and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out to wear down Baby Basma on the descent to the line. Dawn Flame, arriving from just off midfield with Dylan Browne McMonagle driving, could also benefit if the pace is strong enough to bring her into contention.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply in the middle of the race and the hold-up horses find an unobstructed run through the field in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Heart Of Eternity or Variance, operating from their natural off-the-pace position, could pick up the pieces if the front ranks tie each other up and a seam opens late. However, both carry fade warnings and their consistent finishing positions make this scenario structurally fragile even if the pace suits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Baby Basma is bothered early, the pace fragments, and several hold-up horses reach the straight simultaneously having never settled into their preferred rhythm.
scenarios.body: With 16 runners compressed into midfield and no dominant shape imposed, the race devolves into a scramble in which positional luck and draw become decisive. Mini Cotai's trainer form (T14: 3/12) and Wesley Joyce's claim give her a marginal edge in the chaos, though no hold-up horse here has a profile that truly relishes this outcome.

watchPoints.text: Baby Basma is the race-shaper — if Ronan Whelan is allowed to stride clear uncontested at a comfortable tempo, she could prove very difficult to catch at this flat Gowran 7f, and all pace scenarios hinge on what she does in the first two furlongs.

Mini Cotai's trainer Michael Mulvany has three winners from 12 runners in the last 14 days — a hot spell — and Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim gives her a weight edge; watch for market support suggesting the yard fancies this representative.

Dawn Flame ridden by Dylan Browne McMonagle is the most significant jockey booking in the field among the hold-up horses; if the pace is strong enough to bring her into contention from the rear, she represents the most dangerous late threat.

With seven or more genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield positions, traffic and positioning in the straight at Gowran's right-hand final bend could be decisive — horses drawn on the outside or ridden to find clear daylight early in the straight will have a material advantage over those trapped on the inner.|

Stiorra returns from 296 days off and Pocket Jacks from 43 days; monitor both in the pre-race market, as a market move for either would suggest stable confidence that fitness is not an issue, particularly for Stiorra whose absence is otherwise a genuine concern.|

races.name: O'Driscolls Irish Whiskey Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Eichan San
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer whose recent form reads 12/8/11/5/4 over similar trips on Good — no wins or places in this going/distance combination to recommend confidence; Casey is a 7lb claimer and the 37-day break adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: Veteran campaigner who is the race's sole confirmed front-runner, bringing strong similar-going form (14/15) and recent course experience (2nd over 7f Good); tagged STYLE_FIT=0.93 as a P-type, but here that P-style is an asset in a field with minimal early pace.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who tends to fill the rear of the field and has posted predominantly double-figure finishes in recent starts; Ben Coen is strong booking but the horse needs traffic to part ahead of it, a luxury unlikely in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type (age 10) with a blinkers-and-tongue-strap setup, and a notable 2nd over 8f Good in its recent history suggests the horse retains residual ability; Gowran's flat 7f is shorter than preferred distances, but the form profile is the strongest among the true closers.

runners_data.name: The Blue Panther
runners_data.note: Naturally a deep hold-up runner placed in midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed; the 8-year-old's recent Gowran form shows a 4th and the style-fit discount (0.92) applies — true pace position may be harder to find than the map implies.

runners_data.name: Miqdaad
runners_data.note: Carries a "fades in finish" flag and a style-fit warning (0.91), suggesting this horse struggles to deliver its best from the rear in a race that may not generate enough tempo; 58-day absence is a notable additional concern.

runners_data.name: Tariff
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old with only one run at Good going in the last five starts and a wholly poor recent record (0/5 in the form string); the fades-in-finish flag and redistribution from the back of the field make this an unlikely beneficiary of this race shape.

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Prominent-going type with an active stable (T14: 1/3) and course form, showing a 3rd over 7f Good in recent outings; of all the runners likely to press Dynamic Force, this one has the profile to actually secure a forward position and sustain it.

runners_data.name: Leannespour
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old (only 3 career runs, all on Good or Soft) who has finished 11th, 14th, and 15th — deeply unproven and the fades-in-finish flag alongside redistribution leaves little appeal; Declan McDonogh's experience is the lone positive angle.

runners_data.name: Darwin's Angel
runners_data.note: Stepping back from longer trips (10f-12f history) to 7f for the first time in recent races; the going is fine but the trip looks potentially sharp for a horse yet to show winning form, and redistribution away from its natural position further complicates its chance.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Placed twice in five runs on Good going (3rd, 4th) and trained by McGuinness who has been active (3/32 in 14 days); the horse is a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map, and the style-fit figure (0.93) is a discount worth applying.

runners_data.name: Incredible Army
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Standard going (1st) but has not shown that form on Good surfaces (1/7 sim-going), and the 78-day layoff is the longest in the field — the fades-in-finish flag compounds the concern about whether this horse will be ready to fire on return.

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Dropped markedly in class from longer trips (10f-12f) to 7f; Good going is familiar but the fades-in-finish flag and a 2nd over 10f Good as best recent effort suggests the horse lacks the tactical pace to get involved when the race is run at a controlled tempo.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: The most interesting prominent-style runner after Dynamic Force — won over 6f Good, placed 2nd and 3rd multiple times at that trip, and the Magee yard has been in strong form (4/14 in 14 days); stepping to 7f for the first time is a question mark, but the early-pace profile fits this shape.

runners_data.name: Nosmokewithoutfire
runners_data.note: Flagged as fades-in-finish and genuinely a hold-up type displaced into midfield by field congestion; only 2 runs on Good going (finishing 7th and 12th), which alongside the style-fit discount (0.90) makes this horse one of the least well-suited runners to this particular race shape.

runners_data.name: Snap Decision
runners_data.note: Has twice finished 6th on Good going and twice 8th or worse; the fades-in-finish flag, redistribution from its true hold-up position, and a string of 8s and 6s in recent form suggest this horse is currently below the level needed to compete in this grade.

races.paceDynamic: Dynamic Force is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one genuine pace-setter in a 16-runner field, is likely to dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop from the front on Good ground over Gowran's flat 7f. Glen Breeze and Jackandthefox are the most likely candidates to press from prominent positions, meaning the pace should be honest but not brutal — a sustainable tempo that keeps the race together and limits the advantage available to horses coming from off the pace. With the vast majority of this field being natural hold-up horses, many of them have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map simply because the rear is oversubscribed — The Blue Panther, Nosmokewithoutfire, Tariff, Leannespour, Beau Army, Darwin's Angel, Miqdaad and Snap Decision cannot all get their preferred ground at the back, and the most likely beneficiaries of the real estate closest to the pace are those with strong enough early speed to overcome redistribution. This race shape firmly favours horses who can race prominently or in the first half of the field, as a steady pace from one front-runner gives no natural advantage to deep hold-up horses and the final 2f are likely to be run at a sprint that suits those already in position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Dynamic Force dictates a moderate tempo unchallenged and the race is set up for horses travelling prominently from early on.
scenarios.body: Glen Breeze and Jackandthefox are ideally placed just off the pace and can challenge on the bridle as the race develops; a steady gallop means the finish is a sprint the leaders will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Lead Stolen
scenarios.trigger: If Dynamic Force sets a controlled pace and sustains it all the way, proving hard to peg back from the front.
scenarios.body: Dynamic Force's OR=59 profile on similar going (14/15 runs on Good) and recent course form make it competitive if the race is run at its tempo; a hold position becomes a winning position as challengers find insufficient time to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is stronger than expected and a prominent runner fires off too soon, creating a gap for the first finisher from the chasing pack.
scenarios.body: Brains has placed on Good ground and holds solid midfield claims, while Beau Army has the build profile to get closest from a mid-race position; however, most plausible midfield closers here are redistributed hold-up types, reducing the likelihood of a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong, the field strings out, and a true hold-up type finds daylight in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely scenario given a single pace-setter and a field packed with horses who cannot all get their true hold-up position; most tagged hold-up types are redistributed and carry meaningful style-fit discounts.

watchPoints.text: Dynamic Force sets off alone in front — watch how quickly Glen Breeze and Jackandthefox press it at the 5f pole, as any gap in the first quarter could prove decisive for the whole field's positioning.

Glen Breeze steps up to 7f for the first time having won and placed consistently at 6f — if the extra furlong is within its range, it is the single biggest danger to the pace scenario unfolding in the leaders' favour.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (The Blue Panther, Beau Army, Miqdaad, Tariff, Leannespour, Darwin's Angel, Snap Decision, Nosmokewithoutfire) will cause early traffic and crowding — any horse needing a clear run from midfield should be monitored for whether it finds one.
Incredible Army returns after a 78-day layoff; if the Foley yard has it spot-on, the OR=59 rating is competitive, but race-fitness against horses with recent outings is the key watch point.

Brains (age 10) is the most experienced hold-up type in the field and has shown recent ability over 8f Good — worth monitoring whether the 7f trip allows it to get close enough to the pace to challenge, or whether it arrives too late.

races.name: John Fleming Irish EBF Marble City Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Amadeus Mozart
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here, Ronan Whelan should find the lead without resistance; has placed at 1m4f+ on Good ground four times in five and a first career win over this trip last time stamps him as a genuine stayer, though his STYLE_FIT tag suggests his best form has come racing slightly less prominently than a true pace-setter.|

runners_data.name: Echo Inferno
runners_data.note: Won impressively over 1m5f at Leopardstown last time on Good ground giving this field fitness and form credentials, but Shane Foley will find it hard to secure his natural position — a genuine front-runner, he is likely to be crowded back by Amadeus Mozart and Shosholoza's presence and may need to switch tactics entirely to make his influence felt.|

runners_data.name: Nil Bua Gan Dua
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Joseph O'Brien's hold-up specialist who has run in 7 Good-ground races and placed in four; headgear noted and progressive form over 1m3f-1m4f suggests the trip suits well, and he is the most naturally suited of any runner to a genuine end-to-end gallop.|

runners_data.name: Shosholoza
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer for Joseph O'Brien but has failed to trouble the judge in his last three starts, all on Good or similar ground at 1m2f-1m4f; headgear (tongue-tie) worn again and McDonogh takes over — better ground and the step back to basics here may help, but the form line is uninspiring.|

runners_data.name: Believed
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners this J P Murtagh-trained three-year-old who won a Listed 1m4f at Saratoga and has strong Good-ground placed form; naturally wants to race prominently, and the note of caution is that the race shape will likely push him wider and further back than he prefers, making his Listed-class ceiling the only realistic platform.|

runners_data.name: Camino Vino
runners_data.note: Cromwell's filly hasn't run in 54 days and steps up in class from a disappointing run at Leopardstown — the sole previous win came over 1m on Standard ground; a hold-up type who lacks the form credentials at this level but the step to 1m4f on Good ground gives at least a question mark worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Saga Gaga
runners_data.note: Two wins in a row for M D O'Callaghan, the most recent a smooth 1m4f success on Good ground at Leopardstown just 11 days ago; prominently raced and appears to handle the prominent position better than most rivals, making him the freshest form horse in the field with conditions a carbon copy of last time.|

runners_data.name: Vauntingly
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f at Gowran Park recently for Joseph O'Brien and holds a course-and-distance advantage, but a true prominent type who will find Amadeus Mozart, Shosholoza, and Saga Gaga occupying the berths he needs; J M Sheridan would need to manufacture a forward position very early or settle for a role the horse won't relish.|

races.paceDynamic: Amadeus Mozart is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in an 8-runner 1m4f Listed contest on Good ground, he should dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop from the outset. Shosholoza and Saga Gaga are the natural prominent horses likely to sit just behind Amadeus Mozart and complete the early order, with the field stringing out behind them at a controlled tempo. Believed, Echo Inferno, and Vauntingly are all natural prominent types but the field holds more front-running and prominent horses than the race shape can absorb — of these three, Shosholoza and Saga Gaga are best placed to secure their natural berth, while Believed, Echo Inferno, and Vauntingly are most likely to be shuffled back into a midfield they don't naturally occupy. A controlled pace through the first mile at Gowran's flat, galloping track sets up a test of sustained stamina rather than a sprint finish, strongly favouring horses who can travel prominently and quicken from a good position, or those with genuine staying power to reel them in — but a dawdling tempo into the straight will benefit the horse on the speed who can lengthen first.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Amadeus Mozart Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Amadeus Mozart sets an honest but uncontested pace and the race is won by a horse racing in the first three.
scenarios.body: Amadeus Mozart dictates from the front at a sustainable clip, giving Saga Gaga and Shosholoza a comfortable prominent position from which to attack from the turn in; on Good ground over 1m4f at Gowran this is a stamina-speed blend that rewards those able to quicken from a good position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel In Front
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptively quick and horses held up — or pushed back into hold-up roles — finish with momentum in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Nil Bua Gan Dua, a genuine hold-up type with strong Good-ground form at this sort of trip, is best placed among the backmarkers to deliver a sustained late challenge if the pace has been honest enough to soften those up front; Camino Vino is less exposed at this distance and could improve off a big lay-off if the tempo truly burns.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Prominent Gang Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types disrupt early order, creating brief surges that unsettle the rhythm before Amadeus Mozart reasserts.
scenarios.body: Any jostling between Shosholoza, Saga Gaga and the redistributed trio in the early stages could produce an uneven tempo that ultimately still favours those who land a prominent position once order is established; Saga Gaga's recent winning streak and Shosholoza's course-familiar connections make them the likeliest beneficiaries of a race that settles after a scrappy opening.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Overcome Role
scenarios.trigger: If Believed, Echo Inferno, or Vauntingly manage to secure a more forward position than the pace map allows and race to their natural style.
scenarios.body: Despite being mapped back, Believed has Listed-class form over 1m4f+ and if the pace falls away sufficiently for Ben Coen to push forward, the trip and Good ground suit; Vauntingly's recent winning form similarly gives it a live chance if J M Sheridan can find a forward berth in a field that thins early.

watchPoints.text: Saga Gaga arrives on a two-timer, with his most recent win over the identical 1m4f trip and Good ground at Leopardstown — his profile ticks every box for the dominant scenario and he is the horse to beat if the pace is honest.

Amadeus Mozart has the lead to himself but has never won from the front over this trip — watch whether Ronan Whelan allows the race to drift into a falsely slow crawl, which would compress the finish and undermine any hold-up runner's chance.

The cluster of Believed, Echo Inferno, and Vauntingly — all natural front-runners mapped to midfield — creates a risk of interference or traffic issues turning for home if any of them try to push up from their enforced positions.

Nil Bua Gan Dua's booking of Dylan Browne McMonagle is a notable upgrade for the Joseph O'Brien hold-up type, and with seven runs on Good ground and solid placed form over this trip, he is the standout candidate if the pace proves genuinely strong.

Vauntingly's recent Gowran Park course-and-distance win is the only runner with that specific form advantage — monitor any market support at the off, as J M Sheridan knowing the track could help compensate for the tactical disadvantage.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Highway Safety Developments Handicap

runners_data.name: Harana
runners_data.note: Has shown consistent prominent form, placed on good going multiple times and steps back to a mile which suits; Chris Hayes and the powerful Weld yard give confidence, though a five-runner prominent group makes clean positioning critical.

runners_data.name: Frank Pickle
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 8f on good going with Ben Coen up, returning to a distance and surface that produced his last win; held up in a big-field handicap previously so Coen may drop him in early to avoid the prominent congestion, which could actually prove advantageous.

runners_data.name: Ocean Manifest
runners_data.note: Prominent-going type whose last win came over 8f on standard but has done nothing on good going (5th, 10th); the tongue-tie is noted and Jack Kearney's claim reduces weight, but the going record is a genuine worry.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: A 3yo dropping back to a mile, a trip where he has won before; four successive defeats since that win including 8th and 6th on good at Gowran suggest he may need easier conditions, but the promising jockey booking of Dylan Browne McMonagle is a positive flag.

runners_data.name: Hambelton
runners_data.note: The lone genuine front-runner in the field who will get an uncontested lead on good ground over his best trip; his form reads 2-1 at 8f on good and he carries only 129lbs — his entire chance hinges on being allowed to dictate, which the race map strongly suggests he will.

runners_data.name: Snow Princess
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity with only three career runs, all in different conditions, and 101 days off; her running style is unclear and the lengthy absence is a concern, though the relatively light weight of 123lbs means she is not without a chance if fit.

runners_data.name: Red Hugh O'Donnell
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose good-ground form at Gowran is alarming (14th both visits) but whose recent win came on soft; Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim helps on the handicap but this race shape and this track on good ground represent genuine obstacles.

runners_data.name: Zaraahmando
runners_data.note: Useful recent form includes a 2nd and 3rd at 8f on good ground, and trainer-jockey Andrew Slattery doing the double is worth noting; naturally wants to race prominently but is pushed into midfield by the congestion in this field, meaning he will likely race out of his preferred position — temper expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: No More Porter
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran with consistent placing form at 8f on good going (3rd, 2nd, 3rd) who is tough and honest; like Zaraahmando he is a natural prominent runner who will be competing for a midfield berth he does not want — his tenacity in running-on mode is his best asset here.

races.paceDynamic: Hambelton is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, should stride out uncontested from the gates and dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this flat Gowran mile on good ground. Behind him, Harana, Frank Pickle, Ocean Manifest, and Liberation Date all want prominent positions, creating a four-way scramble for the two or three berths available just off the pace — the most dangerous traffic flash-point will come between the two-furlong and three-furlong markers as those horses fight for rail and position. Zaraahmando and No More Porter are genuine prominent types who are unlikely to secure that position in a field this congested, effectively being pushed into a midfield role they would not naturally choose. With Hambelton controlling tempo from the front and the prominent group potentially burning energy jostling for position, this race shape most favours either Hambelton himself travelling cheaply on the lead, or a well-positioned prominent runner who settles cleanly just behind without getting involved in the early scramble.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hambelton Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Hambelton dictates an uncontested, even gallop and has enough in reserve to quicken off his own pace in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Hambelton sets fractions that suit no one else, arriving at the two-furlong pole full of running while the prominent scramblers have wasted energy jostling; his recent win over course and distance on good ground underlines this is his optimal scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Settler Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the early prominent scrimmage for position fractions the group and one well-settled prominent runner tracks Hambelton cleanly before picking him off late.
scenarios.body: The horse that avoids the two-to-three-out traffic fight will have the cleanest passage into the straight and can use Hambelton as a pacemaker to reel in; Frank Pickle's recent course win on good and Ben Coen's positional intelligence make this profile particularly relevant.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the prominent scrimmage creates a true end-to-end gallop that frees up ground for closers.
scenarios.body: Red Hugh O'Donnell, a natural hold-up type with a recent win, would benefit most if the prominent congestion produces a genuinely strong pace; however, his going form on good (14th, 14th at Gowran) tempers confidence considerably.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Rank Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Hambelton is pushed wider than expected and the pace collapses entirely, allowing an unconsidered runner to hold on from a snatched position.
scenarios.body: Snow Princess is unknown in terms of running style and is very lightly raced, meaning she represents the wildcard if the race shape becomes unusually messy or slow; Liberation Date also has the form to capitalise on a muddling gallop having won at this trip before.

watchPoints.text: Harana, Frank Pickle, Ocean Manifest, and Liberation Date all want prominent ground — watch for bumping and checking between the 3f and 2f poles as they battle for the two available berths behind Hambelton; a horse getting squeezed here could lose all chance.

Hambelton's price and probability hinge entirely on being allowed a solo lead — if any of the prominent types is sent forward aggressively from the gates to challenge him, the entire pace map recalibrates and his chance diminishes sharply.

Zaraahmando's trainer-jockey combination (Andrew Slattery, both roles) has had 4 winners from 39 runners over 14 days — a hot strike rate that flags intent, but the horse will likely need to overcome a race position that does not suit its natural style.

Snow Princess returns from 101 days off with no visible market support yet and an undefined running style — any significant market move towards her in the build-up should be treated as a strong stable signal given the absence and the low-key trainer profile.

Red Hugh O'Donnell's form figures of 14-14 on good at Gowran are a clear track-and-going flag; only consider him live if the going softens during the day or if the race develops into a strongly-run affair that neutralises his poor course record.

races.name: Tote Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Burford Beauty
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Gavin Cromwell who has placed at this trip before; 16 days since last run is fine, goes well on good turf (7 turf runs), but has placed only once in her last 10 starts — needs a collapsing pace to fully bring out her best.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here; Denis Gerard Hogan's five-year-old has a clear role advantage as the lone pace-setter and can control every aspect of the gallop — tagged with a style-fit flag because it is technically operating slightly outside its optimal position range, but the lack of rivals to press it makes that largely academic.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns rides the seven-year-old who has a win and two places in his last five on good ground; prefers a trip around 10-12f so this 1m1½f is well within range, and his hold-up style should bring him powerfully into the race from the home turn if the steady Hexagonal-led gallop doesn't rob him of momentum.

runners_data.name: Georg Zhukov
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced four-year-old whose last five runs include very little solid form at this trip on turf — Conor Cusack claims 7lbs, which helps offset the OR of 55; sim-going record is thin (0 wins, 0 places in 4 turf-good starts), and the drop back from 18f to 9f context in his recent history makes pace-reading difficult.

runners_data.name: Haughty
runners_data.note: V C Ward's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer pushed onto the map's midfield section purely by field congestion; the best form shows one win and one place from 15 starts in similar conditions, and the 14-day break is neutral — needs a truly strong pace to fire, which this race may not supply.

runners_data.name: Duchess Anne
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago for Mrs Denise Foster, which raises a freshness flag in a race already stacked with hold-up types; her OR of 40 is among the lowest in the field, and her recent best was a fourth from a hold-up berth — the true rear-of-field style she prefers has been squeezed out of this map by the weight of hold-up horses.

runners_data.name: Jazz Dreamers
runners_data.note: The eight-year-old for Seamus Fahey carries a notable "fades in finish" flag; Patrick McGettigan rides, and recent form shows a 6th from 9 in her last visible result — a horse who drifts right out of contention in the closing stages is poorly served by a slow-run, one-pace finish.

runners_data.name: Lady Luck
runners_data.note: Rodger Sweeney's four-year-old is tagged both as redistributed from the rear and as a horse who fades in finishes — a double flag that markedly limits confidence in a late-run scenario; Julian Pietropaolo (2lb claim) helps marginally, but her 0 wins and 0 places from 11 similar-going starts tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Terry Casey claims 7lbs for Joseph Murray and has run three days ago — that short turnaround warrants attention in a horse who hasn't won in 15 sim-going starts; the hold-up style is his natural habitat but the map has him in midfield given the crowded rear, and recent form of 875750 shows no upward curve.

runners_data.name: Magna Gee Gee
runners_data.note: Patrick Flynn's four-year-old has genuine course-and-distance credentials — a win over 12f on good ground and placed again at the same venue; Robyn Donaghue-Leahy (4lb claim) reduces the weight to a competitive level, and his habit of travelling smoothly from a hold-up position before challenging late gives him a genuine chance even in a steady-run race.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on good ground at his last winning run and has three places from 11 similar-going starts; Richard Brabazon's four-year-old is a natural hold-up horse forced into a midfield position on the map by field numbers, and Jack Cleary will need to decide early whether to push forward — if he does, his cruising speed could make him dangerous in a slow-run scenario.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: W McCreery's eight-year-old has run three days ago and carries a fades-in-finish warning on top of being displaced from his natural rear position by sheer field weight; recent form of 005060 over 8-9f on good ground is discouraging, and Adam Browne-Souza (7lb claim) is the only positive angle.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's four-year-old shows a form string of 699000 and averages a finishing position of 12 from 15 similar-going starts — deeply concerning numbers; tagged as a hold-up type displaced to midfield, and the fades-in-finish flag compounds the style-fit discount to the point where winning in any scenario is a long shot.

runners_data.name: My Vonnie
runners_data.note: M M Rice's five-year-old has exclusively raced on soft/standard surfaces in her last five starts and sim-going data across turf-good is very thin (4 from 15 starts); Rory Mulligan takes the ride and the hold-up style has been pushed to midfield — a genuine unknown on this surface and a step into unfamiliar ground conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Hexagonal is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of 14 and, critically, faces no genuine pace pressure — this sets up a controlled, even gallop from the outset over 1m1½f on good ground at Gowran. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in style, meaning Hexagonal can dictate every yard at a comfortable tempo, conserving energy for a genuine kick in the straight. With no rival capable or likely to challenge for the lead early, the race shape will be strung out from the front, with the pack sitting in behind and committed to a late finishing effort from the home turn. This race shape emphatically favours horses who can travel prominently or produce a sustained, powerful run from just off the pace — pure hold-up types dependent on a true end-to-end gallop to deliver their best will find the tempo insufficient to fully set them alight. The field contains significantly more true hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: of those redistributed to midfield on the map, Yquem, Morning Approach, and Shahada Ace are the ones most likely to attempt to slot into prominent positions ahead of their natural role, though even they face the constraint of Hexagonal's uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hexagonal Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hexagonal secures the lead immediately and controls a moderate, uncontested gallop throughout the 1m1½f trip.
scenarios.body: Hexagonal sets a sustainable pace from the front, ensuring those tracking within two lengths — particularly any runner willing to sit just off the leader — are ideally placed entering the straight; the slow-run nature of the race means class and freshness matter more than pure stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Closer Runs Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that a strong traveller produced late from midfield catches the leader flat-footed in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A truly moderate tempo can paradoxically allow a horse with a high cruising speed to sit a few lengths off the pace and pick off the leader once the straight opens up; on good ground at Gowran, that finish rewards a horse who travels sweetly and has a clean run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If Hexagonal's front-running effort is too taxing and a genuine strong-finishing hold-up type times a run to perfection.
scenarios.body: Should Hexagonal over-extend itself setting even a modest gallop, a fresher closer who gets daylight approaching the final two furlongs can mow down a fading leader; however, most hold-up types in this field are redistributed from their natural position and carry a style-fit discount that reduces the probability of this shape genuinely delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Melee Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If a cluster of pace-hungry horses refuse to settle and create a contested middle section, fragmenting the race shape.
scenarios.body: Several horses tagged as genuine prominent types — Yquem, Morning Approach, Shahada Ace — may push forward unexpectedly, creating brief surges that unsettle the rhythm and open a gap for an opportunist who travels in the right pocket; the disrupted gallop in this scenario could benefit a horse with tactical speed over the final three furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Hexagonal sets the sole pace — watch whether Reese Holohan (4lb claim) can hold a comfortable rhythm in the opening half-mile or is forced to accelerate if any of the redistributed horses (Yquem, Morning Approach) push forward unexpectedly.

Magna Gee Gee's recent course-and-distance win and Robyn Donaghue-Leahy's 4lb claim make this horse a notable danger if she gets a clean passage from midfield turning for home — watch for a run on the inner as the field fans out.

Three runners — Duchess Anne, Master Garvey, Morning Approach — have all raced within three days of this contest; watch for signs of fatigue in the final two furlongs if any of the three are in the mix at the home turn.

Lady Luck and Jazz Dreamers both carry "fades in finish" flags and are displaced from their true hold-up positions — watch whether either drops away sharply in the final furlong, as their lack of a finishing effort could cause interference for horses attempting to come through late.

Georg Zhukov's distance profile is erratic (1f to 18f in recent entries) and Conor Cusack's 7lb claim is relatively inexperienced at this level — watch for positioning errors in the first furlong that could force the horse to race wider than ideal throughout.

races.name: Tote Race

runners_data.name: Benevento
runners_data.note: Lightly used 4-year-old with a hold-up style, trainer Robson De Aguiar in decent recent form (2/16 over 14 days); 161-day absence is a significant concern, and their flat 7f history at this course suggests 1m1½f may stretch them — sim-going record of 7 runs yields just 2 wins and 3 places.|

runners_data.name: Puppet Master
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride for Ciaran Murphy on this 4-year-old who races from the rear, but their five most recent starts are all over hurdle distances (12-17f) making this flat 1m1½f trip a sharp drop in distance that looks awkward — OR of 104 is respectable but the form evidence does not transfer cleanly.|

runners_data.name: Spicy Margarita
runners_data.note: De Aguiar runner reunited with apprentice Paddy Harnett (5lb claim); genuinely a hold-up horse whose last run was just 7 days ago and who has no wins or places from 15 sim-going starts — the fact that they are filling midfield due to field congestion, rather than securing their preferred rear berth, further undermines an already uninspiring record.|

runners_data.name: Ask Me Again
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here, John James Feane's 3-year-old with a tongue strap and a prominent/front-running profile flagged at 0.93 STYLE_FIT; only 2 career starts but gets to dictate on Good ground with no direct pace rival — the class edge over older horses at OR 120 is notable despite the very thin form book.|

runners_data.name: Goddess Of War
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old from the powerful Mrs John Harrington yard with an entirely unknown running style (tagged U) and no last-run date supplied — the going is flagged UNKNOWN for this horse, and with OR 120 matched to Ask Me Again there is a wildcard element, but without form data the risk is substantial.|

runners_data.name: Leopold The First
runners_data.note: Andrew Lee's consistent 4-year-old has finished second in four of his last five starts, always prominent; Robbie Colgan rides and the horse's sim-going record (2/8) confirms they handle Good without issue — the worry is they find a way to get beaten again at the finish despite travelling well.|

runners_data.name: Summer Is Tomorrow
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over on this Joseph O'Brien 3-year-old with a visor, who has a strong recent profile (1W 4P from last 5 on Good) and the in-form trainer's 14-day strike rate of 19/59 is the best in the field — prominent style and genuine distance form at 10f make them one of the better-placed runners for the expected race shape.|

runners_data.name: Hollys Graces
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's 4-year-old is a genuine hold-up type with a hood, returning from 93 days off; Ronan Whelan rides but their record of 0 wins and 0 places from 6 sim-going starts is difficult to overlook — the redistribution to midfield means they are already out of their comfort zone and the layoff adds further doubt.|

races.paceDynamic: Ask Me Again is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 8-runner field over 1m1½f at Gowran on Good ground, and with no genuine rival to push the pace from the front, they are likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo. Summer Is Tomorrow, Leopold The First and Goddess Of War are all prominent-style runners who will contest the positions just off the leader, creating a settled but not slow early gallop. The redistribution note is relevant here: Spicy Margarita and Hollys Graces are genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield simply because the rear of the field is congested with closers — they are unlikely to secure their natural late-run position in this race shape and their chances in a scenario dependent on that role must be discounted accordingly. The overall shape — a single unhurried pace-setter with a cluster of prominent racers tracking close — favours horses who can race prominently and produce a turn-of-foot from a tracking position, rewarding those with a clean run in the final two furlongs rather than those requiring a strong gallop to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Ask Me Again sets an uncontested honest gallop and the prominent trackers Summer Is Tomorrow and Leopold The First get a clean passage into the straight.
scenarios.body: Ask Me Again dictates the fractions from the front, and the prominent types sitting just behind have enough energy in reserve to challenge off a steady tempo; Summer Is Tomorrow's consistent second-place finishes and good-ground form at this distance make them the obvious beneficiary. Leopold The First's relentless place record (2-2-2-2-2 recently) signals they rarely get beaten far when prominent, and this straightforward shape suits that relentless travelling style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ask Me Again is allowed to build a lead unchallenged and the gallop is slow enough that no prominent tracker has the pace to reel them in.
scenarios.body: Ask Me Again, uncontested from the front with a young rider who can conserve energy early, simply never comes off the bridle and the field is strung out behind; the modest pace means those tracking never generate enough momentum. The 3-year-old's OR of 120 gives them a significant class edge and on Good ground with no pressure, they have every chance of lasting.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Summer Is Tomorrow or Leopold The First push the pace too hard tracking Ask Me Again, burning out the prominent group and leaving the race to those held up.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong early tempo between Ask Me Again and the prominent group would burn through the field, leaving the true hold-up horses Benevento and Puppet Master with the gap they need to come through late. Benevento has some place form at similar distances on Good and Puppet Master, though their recent form over hurdles distances looks a mismatch here, could benefit if the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Bunching
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant positional jostling early from the multiple prominent types and the race is run at an irregular, uneven gallop creating a compressed finish.
scenarios.body: With Summer Is Tomorrow, Leopold The First, Goddess Of War and Ask Me Again all wanting prominent berths, a brief scramble for position could lead to a muddling pace and a tight bunched finish in which any horse with residual energy gets a chance; Goddess Of War is lightly raced with unknown profile and could exploit any confusion. Spicy Margarita and Hollys Graces, though mapped out of natural role, could land a blow if the finish is compressed enough that position becomes irrelevant.

watchPoints.text: Summer Is Tomorrow and Leopold The First are both prominent-style runners who will contest the same berths directly behind Ask Me Again — watch for early jostling between them from stalls to the first bend that could unsettle either or compromise their position.

Goddess Of War is completely unknown quantity with no running style, no last-run date and going tagged UNKNOWN — if this horse is well prepared by Harrington and steps forward on debut or return, the market move will be the only warning available.

Ask Me Again's front-running role rests entirely on the field allowing them to dictate — if Leopold The First or Summer Is Tomorrow press them earlier than expected, the pace could become genuinely strong and undermine Ask Me Again's ability to last home.

Benevento's 161-day absence for a hold-up horse who needs a strong pace to deliver their run makes them vulnerable in this race shape — monitor their market move as any support would be surprising given the fitness question and the likely controlled tempo.

Spicy Margarita runs just 7 days after their last outing and sits in a midfield berth that is not their natural position — if they do get shuffled back into their true hold-up role early, they have the worst sim-going record in the field to justify optimism from that position.
